note: Authored by reading Tafsir al-Tabari in English against the reader's modern translation. Each phrase carries the app's own words for that piece of the verse, a plain modern English line of my own, the Arabic of the piece, and the numbered paragraphs of the commentary that speak of it.

phrases.translation: By the night when it covers
phrases.text: God swears by the night when it covers the day with its darkness, so that its light vanishes and its darkness comes on.

phrases.translation: and the day when it shines
phrases.text: This too is an oath, by the day when it grows bright and clear and breaks through, when the darkness of the night no longer stands between it and being seen. Qatada says God swears by these things only because of how great they are to Him.

phrases.translation: And by ˹the One˺ Who created male and female
phrases.text: The word can be read as an oath by God, the Creator of the male and the female, or as an oath by His creation of them. Ibn Masud and Abu al-Darda read it as the male and the female, and Abu al-Darda heard that from the Prophet himself.

phrases.translation: Surely the ends you strive for are diverse
phrases.text: Your deeds run in different directions. Among you is one who disbelieves his Lord and disobeys Him, and one who believes in Him and obeys Him. This answers the oath.

phrases.translation: As for the one who is charitable, mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.text: The one among you who gives in the way of God, spending what God has given him out of His bounty, and who fears God and keeps away from what He has forbidden. Ibn Abbas says he gave what he had and feared his Lord.

phrases.translation: and ˹firmly˺ believes in the finest reward
phrases.text: The commentators differed: some said he believes in the recompense of God for his spending, others that he believes in the oneness of God, others in the Garden. Tabari takes the recompense, and the Prophet said that two angels call out at every sunset, asking God to give the one who spends.

phrases.translation: We will facilitate for them the Way of Ease
phrases.text: We shall make him fit for ease, that is, for the doing of what pleases God in this world, so that He may give him the Garden in the Hereafter.

phrases.translation: And as for the one who is stingy, indifferent ˹to Allah˺
phrases.text: The one who is miserly in spending on God's path, refusing to spend what God has given him, and who thinks himself independent of his Lord and does not long for him by working for him. Ibn Abbas says whoever God enriched and who then withholds the obligatory alms.

phrases.translation: and ˹staunchly˺ denies the finest reward
phrases.text: The commentators differed here as they did about the opposite verse: some said he denies the recompense, some that he denies the oneness of God, some that he denies the Garden. Tabari takes the recompense.

phrases.translation: We will facilitate for them the path of hardship
phrases.text: We shall prepare him in this world for the difficult state, and the hardship is the doing of what God hates. The Prophet said that each person's place in the Garden or the Fire is already written, yet we must still work, for to each one it is made easy, and he recited these verses.

phrases.translation: And their wealth will be of no benefit to them when they tumble ˹into Hell˺
phrases.text: What will this wealth ward off for the man who was stingy with it? Some said the word means when he falls into the Fire, and some said when he dies. Tabari takes the Fire, because that is the well-known sense of the word.
phrases.ar: وَمَا يُغۡنِي عَنۡهُ مَالُهُۥٓ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰٓ

phrases.translation: It is certainly upon Us ˹alone˺ to show ˹the way to˺ guidance
phrases.text: It is for us to make clear the truth from falsehood and obedience from disobedience. The philologists read it as: the way of whoever walks the straight path belongs to God, who is the one who directs the straight way.

phrases.translation: And surely to Us ˹alone˺ belong this life and the next
phrases.text: To us belongs the dominion over this world and the Hereafter. We give of it to whom we will and withhold it from whom we will, honouring the one and humbling the other.

phrases.translation: And so I have warned you of a raging Fire
phrases.text: So I have warned you, O people, of a Fire that blazes up, the Fire of Hell. Beware of disobeying your Lord in this world, so that you do not enter it in the Hereafter and roast in it.

phrases.translation: in which none will burn except the most wretched—
phrases.text: No one will enter it and burn in its blazing fire except the most wretched.

phrases.translation: who deny and turn away
phrases.text: The one who denied the signs of his Lord, turned away from them, and did not hold them to be true. Some grammars say there was no open denial, but that he fell short in the obedience he was commanded, and that was reckoned as denial.

phrases.translation: But the righteous will be spared from it—
phrases.text: The God-fearing one will be kept safe from the burning of that blazing Fire.

phrases.translation: who donate ˹some of˺ their wealth only to purify themselves
phrases.text: The one who spends his wealth in this world on the rights God has laid down for him, and purifies himself of his sins by that giving.

phrases.translation: not in return for someone’s favours
phrases.text: No one has with him a favour he must repay. He spends nothing as a return to a person for some favour done for him, but within the rights of God. It was revealed about Abu Bakr, who had set free people from whom he asked neither repayment nor thanks.
phrases.ar: وَمَا لِأَحَدٍ عِندَهُۥ مِن نِّعۡمَةٖ تُجۡزَىٰٓ

phrases.translation: but seeking the pleasure of their Lord, the Most High
phrases.text: Except that he gives in seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High.

phrases.translation: They will certainly be pleased
phrases.text: This man, who spends his wealth on the rights of God and purifies himself, will surely be content with the reward by which God will recompense him in the Hereafter for what he spent on his path.
